thread:
maya: Heads-up: Cost dashboard shows per-model unit cost swinging wildly after routing retries. Suspect were not slicing cache credits by executed token spans.

devon: Can you drop a tiny repro? is this sticky session + reroute, or merged short sessions?

maya: Sticky. session warmed prefetch_kv=96 on model=fast-bert, then router retried and ~30 tokens executed on slow-bert. dashboard applied the full prefetch credit across all tokens.

maya: ```
session=xyz-004
start_model=fast-bert
prefetch_kv=96
tokens_total=200
reroute_at_token=170
fallback_model=slow-bert
```

piper: We currently add prefetch credit to session-level row at ingest. No token-range bookkeeping. That explains the overcrediting.

pm-rene: For UX we want: a) a reconciliation badge ("provisional / reconciled"), b) a "trace" action that opens the raw routing spans, and c) a tiny confidence score when heuristics are used.

devon: Two engineering paths: 1) router emits compact span events with token_start/token_end/model/prefetch_at_warm, 2) router emits a single handoff_token_index on a handoff event. The latter is lower bandwidth.

maya: prefer handoff_token_index. Minimal surface: telemetry event session_handoff {session_id, handoff_token_index, prefetch_kv}. Billing can prorate credits by token index.

piper: Agree. Fallback: for old routers estimate handoff via timestamps + mean tokens/sec and mark as estimated in UI.

devon: Debate: sync header (x-handoff-token) vs async telemetry event. Headers are immediate for sync consumers but couple router to billing. Events are more flexible.

pm-rene: From product POV, events are ok as long as console marks numbers provisional until reconciled and shows the event IDs in drilldown.

maya: Implementation sketch: router -> emits session_handoff event at handoff; telemetry indexer writes to session_spans table; billing joins tokenized usage to session_spans for final allocation; console shows provisional numbers and then swaps to reconciled after nightly job.

piper: Need tests: - handoff inside a chunk (non-aligned offset), - multiple consecutive handoffs, - legacy router with heuristic fallback. I'll add integration vectors.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout starting for router-handoff-event -> 2/5 hosts updated :rocket:

devon: UX tweak: timeline sparkline on tenant/detail that overlays the model spans and shades credited area. Tooltip shows metadata: prefetch_kv, handoff_idx, event_id, and a link to logs.

pm-rene: Also surface estimated error: e.g. "est. B1 9% (heuristic)" for any allocations using timestamp heuristics. And allow toggling to hide provisional numbers in admin view.

maya: Timeline: router event + indexer = 1d, billing join + nightly reconcile = 2d, console UX + feature flag = 1.5d. Prioritize landing a test vector that reproduces negative savings in top-ten.

piper: Will write a small integration test and a unit test for prorating math. Edgecase: fractional KV credits when handoff splits inside a token-chunk; billing must handle rounding consistently.

devon: Reassigning to eng-platform. Please bump the FF in rollout doc when tests land.

maya: I'll open the PR with the telemetry schema + test vectors and ping here. Closing once PR merged and FF gated successful canary. Thanks! :thumbsup:
